questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is the most common cause of excessive daytime sleepiness?
questions.explanation:
Sleep apnoea accounts for 43.2% of disorders associated with excessive daytime sleepiness.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 731

questions.question_text: The antidepressant that does not suppress REM sleep is
questions.explanation:
Bupropion does not suppress REM sleep, and neither does nefazodone.
Comprehensive text book of psychiatry,8 the edition,p-294

questions.question_text: Sudden arousal from sleep with intense fearfulness, which may begin with scream or cry is associated with
questions.explanation:
Sleep terror is characterized by sudden arousal with intense fearfulness, which may begin with a piercing scream or cry.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 737

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a common feature of Narcolepsy?
questions.explanation:
Hypnopompic hallucinations are not commonly seen in narcolepsy
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 723

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following does NOT predispose to Obstructive sleep apnoea?
questions.explanation:
Hypothyroidism and acromegaly are predisposing factors for obstructive sleep apnea. Hyperthyroidism is not.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 732

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following sleep abnormalities is NOT seen in depression?

options.text: Lengthening of latency to REM sleep
Occurrence of REM sleep earlier in the night
Increase in slow-wave sleep in the first non-rapid eye movement (NREM)-rapid eye movement (REM) cycle

correct_answer.text: Lengthening of latency to REM sleep

correct_answers.text: Lengthening of latency to REM sleep

questions.explanation:
REM latency is shortened, not lengthened, in sleep disturbances in depressed patients.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-385

questions.question_text: A lady with multiple sclerosis presents with depression. The drug most likely to be the cause is:
questions.explanation:
Use of interferon beta is associated with depression and suicidal thoughts; these conditions are also more common with MS. Any symptoms of depression should be immediately reported - patients should be made aware that depression and/or suicidal thoughts may occur with interferon beta.
Expert Opin Drug Saf. 2007 May;6(3):279-88.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following symptoms is LESS likely to be associated with temporal lobe tumors than Schizophrenia?
questions.explanation:
Flat or inappropriate affect, a classic symptom of schizophrenia, is not seen in patients with temporal lobe tumors; rather, these patients often exhibit a broad range of affect and appropriate interpersonal behaviour.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 279

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT true about memory deficits in schizophrenia?

options.text: Patients frequently exhibit disorganized or inefficient retrieval strategies
Procedural learning is usually intact with few or no deficits
Deficits are more pronounced in tests of recognition than in tests of recall
Patients usually have little or no deficits in nondeclarative memory tests
Patients have shallow or inefficient encoding of information

correct_answer.text: Deficits are more pronounced in tests of recognition than in tests of recall

correct_answers.text: Deficits are more pronounced in tests of recognition than in tests of recall

questions.explanation:
Declarative memory deficits in schizophrenia are usually more pronounced in tests of recall than in tests of recognition.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-779

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most common in delirium?
questions.explanation:
Common features of a delirious state are clouding of consciousness, altered sleep wake cycle, agitation/overactive state or underactive/drowsy state and impaired cognition.
Textbook of Organic Psychiatry

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a symptom of orbitofrontal syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Perseveration is not a characteristic of orbitofrontal syndrome, but is seen with injury to the dorsolateral frontal cortex.
Core psychiatry,2 edition, Wright ,stern & Phelan,p-384

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is a feature of dorsolateral prefrontal syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Dorsolateral prefrontal syndrome is associated with executive dysfunction such as poor initiation of tasks and impaired working memory.
Core psychiatry,2 edition, Wright ,stern & Phelan,p-384

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT commonly observed in amnesic patients?
questions.explanation:
Aphasia is not a clinical characteristic typically found in amnesic patients.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 8

questions.question_text: Depressed patients are more likely to have deficits in which of the following domains than nondepressed patients?
questions.explanation:
In general, depressed patients are more likely to manifest deficits on tasks that require effort or greater depth of processing, but not on tasks that can be completed automatically.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-28

questions.question_text: Which drug given prophylactically is shown to decrease delirium:
questions.explanation:
Prophylactic haloperidol has been shown to reduce the incidence of delirium.
Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, Volume 54,Number 5, May 2006 , pp. 860-861

questions.question_text: Which of the following treatments for multiple sclerosis is most likely to lead to depression?
questions.explanation:
Use of interferon beta is associated with depression and suicidal thoughts; these conditions are also more common with MS.
Expert Opin Drug Saf. 2007 May;6(3):279-88.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the best evidence base for its use in post-stroke depression?
questions.explanation:
Randomized controlled trials have demonstrated the efficacy of sertraline, citalopram and nortriptyline to treat post-stroke depression.
Expert Opin Pharmacother. 2008 May;9(8):1291-8.

questions.question_text: The recommended treatment for pathological crying is:
questions.explanation:
Three cases of successful treatment of pathological crying using the SSRI citalopram are reported.
Pharmacopsychiatry. 2001 Nov;34(6):254-8

questions.question_text: The most common disorder associated with resting tremor is
questions.explanation:
Parkinson's disease is the most common disorder associated with rest tremor.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-939

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a common comorbidity of Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation:
Obsessive-compulsive disorder is infrequently comorbid with Huntington's disease.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 470-2

questions.question_text: The psychiatric disorder most commonly found in patients with Parkinson's disease is
questions.explanation:
Affective disorder is the most common psychiatric disturbance in Parkinson's disease, with an estimated incidence of from 20% to 90%.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-736

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT found in diffuse Lewy body disease?
questions.explanation:
Apathy is not a clinical characteristic of diffuse Lewy body disease.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-936

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following terms describes sudden jerks, sometimes simple, but sometimes as complex as well-organized voluntary movements, that may be temporarily relieved during sleep or when concentrating on an enjoyable task?
questions.explanation:
Tics are sudden jerks which can be simple or as complex as organized voluntary movements, such as touching an object or speaking a word.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-949

questions.question_text: The following clinical finding is helpful in distinguishing progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) from Parkinson's disease?
questions.explanation:
PSP may be distinguished from Parkinson's disease by axial parkinsonism without tremor, unstable gait with postural instability, and vertical eye movement abnormalities.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-936

questions.question_text: Wilson's disease is associated with abnormal liver function and degeneration of which ONE of the following regions?
questions.explanation:
In Wilson's disease, also called hepatolenticular degeneration, the basal ganglia degenerate in association with abnormalities in liver function.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 662

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a lower motor neurone lesion?
questions.explanation:
Pseudobulbar palsy is an upper motor neurone lesion, not a lower motor neurone lesion.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 338

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following antidepressants should be avoided in depression secondary to HIV/AIDS?
questions.explanation:
Nefazodone should be avoided in HIV/AIDS patients because of its affinity for cytochrome P450 (leading to drug–drug interactions) and its propensity to cause hepatotoxicity.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-1025

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is the commonest CNS neoplasm in patients with HIV/AIDS?
questions.explanation:
Primary B-cell non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma is the commonest CNS neoplasm in patients with HIV/AIDS.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 320

questions.question_text: The most common opportunistic infection in AIDS, which may present as a focal or diffuse cognitive or affective disturbance, is
questions.explanation:
Toxoplasma gondii is the most common opportunistic infection in AIDS and may present as a focal or diffuse cognitive or affective disturbance.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 320

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following stages of sleep does NOT correspond to its characteristic EEG feature?

options.text: Stage 2 – sleep spindles and K complexes

questions.explanation:
Alpha activity, not beta, is the characteristic EEG feature of stage 0 sleep (transition from wakefulness to sleep).
NMS Physiology, 2 edition P79

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the EEG in cognitive disorders is true?

options.text: Mild diffuse slowing is pathological in individuals older than 75 years.
EEG slowing is correlated with the severity of dementia and the number of senile plaques in Alzheimer's disease.
Focal delta activity in the anterior temporal areas is rare in patients older than 60 years.
A drop in background alpha of 1–2 Hz over a short period is not indicative of delirium as long as the alpha rhythm remains in the normal range.
Low-voltage beta activity increases in adults up to age 60 years and remains stable thereafter.

correct_answer.text: EEG slowing is correlated with the severity of dementia and the number of senile plaques in Alzheimer's disease.

correct_answers.text: EEG slowing is correlated with the severity of dementia and the number of senile plaques in Alzheimer's disease.

questions.explanation:
EEG slowing has been found to correlate with the severity of dementia and the number of senile plaques in Alzheimer's disease.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 439

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following EEG changes occurs with use of tricyclic antidepressants?
questions.explanation:
Tricyclic antidepressants increase delta, theta and beta rhythms on the EEG.
Revision notes in Psychiatry,P 144-5

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following EEG changes is associated with the use of benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation:
Benzodiazepines reduce the alpha rhythm and increase beta and theta rhythms on the EEG.
Revision notes in Psychiatry,P 144-5

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following EEG changes is caused by antipsychotics?
questions.explanation:
Antipsychotics increase beta, theta and delta rhythms on the EEG.
Revision notes in Psychiatry,P 144-5

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following electroencephalography (EEG) frequency ranges is NOT correct?
questions.explanation:
Theta range is 4–8 Hz, not less than 1 Hz.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3rd Edition P 127

questions.question_text: Diagnostic features of neurasthenia include the following EXCEPT

options.text: Duration of the disorder is at least 6 months

correct_answer.text: Duration of the disorder is at least 6 months

correct_answers.text: Duration of the disorder is at least 6 months

questions.explanation: According to ICD-10, the duration of neurasthenia must be at least 3 months, not 6 months.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following would LOWER your suspicions of brain tumour in a patient with behavioural symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Nonfocal neurological signs are not indicative of a brain tumour.
--

questions.question_text: Trance-like states are more common with which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation:
Temporal lobe neoplasms are most commonly associated with trance-like states and complex behavioural disturbances.
NMS Psychiatry,3 Edn,P-133,140

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is true about working memory?

options.text: Is a form of declarative memory
Is similar to what in the past was called long-term memory
Is viewed as a single memory buffer
Is a form of nondeclarative memory
Has the central executive as its most important component

correct_answer.text: Has the central executive as its most important component

correct_answers.text: Has the central executive as its most important component

questions.explanation:
The central executive is the most important component of working memory, coordinating information from separate subsystems.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-33-34

questions.question_text: The dementia syndrome, characterized by fluctuating symptom severity, visual hallucinations, attentional impairment, altered consciousness, and delusions, particularly difficult to distinguish from delirium is
questions.explanation:
Lewy body dementia mimics delirium in its characteristic fluctuations in symptoms over time.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 450-1

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a feature of Frontal Lobe Syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Hemispheric neglect is seen with parietal lobe lesions, not frontal lobe syndrome.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 76-77

questions.question_text: Abulia may be defined as

options.text: The patient's continuing into present activity the elements of previous actions
The patient's automatic repetition of his or her own word or phrase
The patient's incapacity to sustain activities that he or she was quite capable of beginning
The patient's lack of will, which in less severe form may include slowness, delayed response, laconic speech, and reduced initiative and effort
The patient's incapacity to carry out a sequential or ordered set of actions toward a unitary goal in the presence of the necessary objects

correct_answer.text: The patient's lack of will, which in less severe form may include slowness, delayed response, laconic speech, and reduced initiative and effort

correct_answers.text: The patient's lack of will, which in less severe form may include slowness, delayed response, laconic speech, and reduced initiative and effort

questions.explanation:
Abulia, or lack of will, describes loss of spontaneity and initiative due to cerebral disease.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 214

questions.question_text: One of the following is not a feature of chronic fatigue syndrome

options.text: Feeling tired after rest, relaxation and enjoyment

correct_answer.text: Feeling tired after rest, relaxation and enjoyment

correct_answers.text: Feeling tired after rest, relaxation and enjoyment

questions.explanation:
Chronic fatigue syndrome is characterised by fatigue, post-exertional malaise, sleep dysfunction, pain, neurological/cognitive, autonomic, neuroendocrine and immune manifestations; fatigue is not relieved by rest.
Oxford textbook of Psychiatry, 4th edition, 2001

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is an autosomal recessively inherited degenerative dementia?
questions.explanation:
Wilson's disease is autosomal recessively inherited.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 662

questions.question_text: Palilalia is

options.text: The patient's repetition of speech of another person
The patient's automatic repetition of his or her own word or phrase
Loss of the production or recognition of affective elements of speech
A disorder of fluency in which discourse is disturbed by deficits in speech pragmatics, motor control, and attention
The patient's speech marked by impulsive utterances of stereotyped or simple responses with no aphasic or echolalic features

correct_answer.text: The patient's automatic repetition of his or her own word or phrase

correct_answers.text: The patient's automatic repetition of his or her own word or phrase

questions.explanation:
Palilalia is the automatic repetition of the patient's own words or phrases.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-949

questions.question_text: The Frontal Assessment Battery primarily assesses
questions.explanation:
The FAB was devised to identify executive dysfunction at the bedside.
Dubois B, Slachevsky A, Litvan I, et al: The FAB: a Frontal Assessment Battery at bedside. Neurology 55:1621-1626, 2000

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is true regarding dissociative amnesia?

options.text: It usually interferes with social or occupational functioning
It is more common in the elderly than in adolescents or young adults
It is more common in males
It is frequently diagnosed, especially among patients with "hysterical" disorders

questions.explanation:
Dissociative amnesia is usually transient; most cases show rapid recovery of memory.
Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edition, p481

questions.question_text: Tumour of which of the following areas causes bitemporal hemianopsia, optic atrophy, and diabetes insipidus?
questions.explanation:
Clinical signs associated with pituitary tumors include bitemporal hemianopsia, optic atrophy, hypopituitarism, and diabetes insipidus.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 229-230

questions.question_text: You have a female patient with hepatic encephalopathy now presenting with increased sexual drive and carbohydrate craving. She has:
questions.explanation:
Kluver–Bucy syndrome results from temporal lobe damage and is characterised by hyperorality, hypersexuality, and disinhibition.
--

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a test of executive function?
questions.explanation:
All the listed tests assess executive functions.
Text book of Neuropsychiatry,2 edition, Schiffer,Rao,Fogel,p-334

questions.question_text: Huntington's disease shows which pattern of inheritance?
questions.explanation:
Huntington's disease is autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
Oxford textbook of Psychiatry, 4th edition, 2001

questions.question_text: A 40 year old farmer comes to see you with general malaise, low mood, and a circumscribed 4cm red lesion on his chest. You diagnose:
questions.explanation:
The acute phase of Lyme disease infection is a characteristic reddish "bulls-eye" rash, with accompanying fever, malaise, and musculoskeletal pain (arthralgia or myalgia).[1] The characteristic reddish "bull's-eye" rash (known as erythema migrans) may be seen in about 80% of early stage Lyme
www.medicinenet.com/lyme_disease

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following classes of medication do NOT cause memory impairment?
questions.explanation:
it appears that atypical antipsychotic agents have an ameliorative effect on cognitive deficits in schizophrenia, with risperidone exerting stronger beneficial effects on working (short-term) memory and olanzapine exerting stronger action on verbal learning and memory.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 54-5

questions.question_text: Cerebellar lesions can cause
questions.explanation:
Cerebellar lesions cause physical signs and impairment in higher order functioning - for example, intention tremor, impaired alternating movements (dysdiadokinesis), personality change, ataxia.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 230-1

questions.question_text: In testing for which primitive reflex does the examiner bring the reflex hammer toward the patient's mouth, then to the side?
questions.explanation:
Rooting is assessed by bringing an object, such as a reflex hammer, toward a patient's mouth and then to the side.
Macleod's clinical examination,11 edition,p-360

questions.question_text: Lesions in the parietal lobe can cause
questions.explanation:
Apraxia occurs in parietal lobe lesions
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 17-18

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is NOT a component of Gerstmann's syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Hemi-neglect is not a feature of Gerstmann's syndrome.
Organic Psychiatry,Lishman,3 rd Edition P 65

questions.question_text: What treatment has the most evidence for depression following a myocardial infarction:
questions.explanation:
The Sertraline Anti-Depressant Heart Attack Trial (SADHAT) study was an investigator-initiated, open-label, clinical trial conducted in US. This study concluded that Sertraline was an effective treatment for post MI depression
Am Heart J 137(6):1100-1106, 1999. 1999

questions.question_text: A 25 year old air hostess has problems with her job due to daytime sleepiness. She has difficulty with sleeping at night, but reports no other symptoms
questions.explanation: 1. B. Long-haul flights disrupt circadian rhythm.

questions.question_text: A 40 year old man has trouble with excessive day time sleepiness. His wife has complained that she has to sleep in another room due to his loud snoring at night. She has also heard him gasp for breath on a few occasions
questions.explanation: 2. F. The noisy breathing indicates obstructive sleep apnoea.

questions.explanation: 3. C – A flapping tremor is characteristic of hepatic encephalopathy.

questions.question_text: A woman taking St John’s Wort who becomes pregnant in spite of taking the oral contraceptive pill.
questions.explanation: 1. D. St John‘s Wort is an enzyme inducer and thereby reduces plasma levels of drugs that are metabolised by the P450 system.

questions.question_text: A man who is on a typical antipsychotic and develops EPSE.

questions.question_text: A woman taking fluoxetine who is commenced on amitriptyline. She becomes confused, agitated and exhibits myoclonus.
questions.explanation: 3. I. This scenario describes serotonin syndrome. 5HT2 receptors may be involved in this. Serotonin syndrome is a toxic state caused mainly by excess serotonin within the central nervous system. It results in a variety of mental, autonomic and neuromuscular changes, which can range in severity from mild to life-threatening. Most cases are self-limiting. Severe serotonin syndrome is nearly always caused by a drug interaction involving two or more 'serotonergic' drugs, at least one of which is usually a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or monoamine oxidase inhibitor.

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding Acamprosate.

options.text: act as an agonist at NMDA receptors
Can be used with controlled drinking

questions.explanation:
Acamprosate works by reducing the craving for alcohol. It seems to involve the restoration of NMDA receptor tone in glutaminergic systems
Glutamatergic Neurotransmission in Alcoholism. J Biomed Sci 1998;5:309-320

questions.question_text: Resilience is

options.text: different from protective factors, which increase the chances of a child being more resilient
a process that is rarely open to influence
a static trait, internal to the individual
a defence mechanism created by a child who feels worthless, unwanted and lacks confidence
extremely difficult to encourage if it is not there innately

correct_answer.text: different from protective factors, which increase the chances of a child being more resilient

correct_answers.text: different from protective factors, which increase the chances of a child being more resilient

questions.explanation:
There seem to be factors and processes that can minimise the negative impact of parental drug or alcohol misuse, or protect against them. Thus, some children are resilient and develop no significant problems related to their parents' substance misuse. Resilience should be conceptualised as a process, rather than a static trait and/or something solely internal to the individual.
Velleman & Templeton (2007) Adv Psych Treat 13:79-89

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Cocaine acts primarily on the 5-HT system
Cannabinoids bind to the GABA receptor
PCP acts on the glutamate receptor

correct_answer.text: PCP acts on the glutamate receptor

correct_answers.text: PCP acts on the glutamate receptor

questions.explanation:
Cocaine blocks dopamine uptake at the dopamine re-uptake site. Hallucinogens act at multiple sites, but the effects are thought to be related to 5-HT antagonism. MDMA is a hallucinogenic amphetamine. Cannabis has anticholinergic effects, and its action is particularly marked in the hippocampus.
Seeman et al (2005) Molecular Psychiatry 10(9): 877-883

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a complication of alcohol misuse?
questions.explanation:
Alcohol affects all systems of body and causes a multitude of physical, psychiatric and social complications
Revision Notes in Psychiatry - Puri & Hall, 2nd Edition (2004) p336-340

questions.question_text: In relation to the evidence that cannabis use may cause psychotic illness, which ONE of the following statements is true?

options.text: in several studies, increased frequency of reported cannabis use has been associated with increased reporting of unusual thoughts and perceptions
confounding occurs when people exaggerate both their use of cannabis and their experience of psychotic symptoms
several large prospective studies among young people in the general population have shown cannabis use to be associated with increased diagnosis of schizophrenia
it is likely that the association between cannabis use and psychotic symptoms seen in several studies has arisen by chance
the fact that there are plausible neurophysiological mechanisms through which cannabis use might cause psychosis is probably the strongest evidence that it does

correct_answer.text: in several studies, increased frequency of reported cannabis use has been associated with increased reporting of unusual thoughts and perceptions

correct_answers.text: in several studies, increased frequency of reported cannabis use has been associated with increased reporting of unusual thoughts and perceptions

questions.explanation:
Since the late 1960s cannabis use has increased substantially in most high-income countries (Hickman et al, 2007). The increase may now be levelling off, but this is hardly a reason for complacency.
Cannabis is now well established as the third most widely used psychoactive drug (after alcohol and tobacco) in Europe, the USA and Australasia (Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs, 2006). In the UK around half of adolescents will use cannabis at least once and about a fifth of them will use it regularly (monthly or more frequently) in young adulthood.
Macleod (2007) Adv Psych Treat 13: 400-411

questions.question_text: You see a 45 year old man in A&E who admits to drinking 8 pints of lager a day for the past 20 years. He recognises that this may be causing him physical and psychological problems, but is not sure that he wants to change his drinking pattern yet. What stage is he at on Prochaska and DiClemente's model of Stages of Change?
questions.explanation:
The Prochaska and DiClemente model, developed over the past 20 years, identifies 5 stages: precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action, and maintenance. It covers a cycle of attitudes from denial to secure, solidly established commitment to change. In the precontemplation stage, people are not thinking seriously about changing and are not interested in any kind of help. In the contemplation stage people are more aware of the personal consequences of their bad habit and they spend time thinking about their problem. Although they are able to consider the possibility of changing, they tend to be ambivalent about it.
Prochaska JO, DiClemente CC, Norcross JC. In search of how people change. Am Psychol 1992;47:1102-4.

questions.question_text: You are called to A&E to see a man withdrawing from amphetamines. Which of the following is he least likely to exhibit:
questions.explanation:
Amphetamine withdrawal is associated with agitation, depression, insomnia and loss of appetite called crash.
Oxford textbook of Psychiatry, 4th edition, 2001

questions.question_text: In relation to interventions to prevent drug use among young people, which ONE of the following is true?

options.text: school-based educational interventions appear very effective in reducing young people's drug use
school-based interventions may occasionally have unexpected adverse effects
there is no evidence that motivational interviewing is effective as an intervention to reduce drug use
one of the most effective prevention strategies seems to be the prohibition of drugs such as cannabis
reductions in drug use seen with school-based educational campaigns may be small but tend to be sustained over several years

correct_answer.text: school-based interventions may occasionally have unexpected adverse effects

correct_answers.text: school-based interventions may occasionally have unexpected adverse effects

questions.explanation:
Criminal justice-based interventions appear politically popular and should not be dismissed out of hand. However, they seem likely to fail in relation to all these requirements. School-based educational interventions are also popular, and may be more acceptable and humane. They can, however, still have unexpected adverse effects (Aveyard et al, 1999). They are also expensive and, currently, appear to have limited long-term positive effects (White & Pitts, 1998; Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs, 2006).
Macleod (2007) Adv Psych Treat 13: 400-411

questions.question_text: A man who drinks two bottles of vodka a day tries to stop by himself. He is brought into hospital with ataxia, and confusion. The chances that he will develop Korsakoff's Psychosis are:
questions.explanation:
Approximately 80 to 90 percent of alcoholics with Wernicke's encephalopathy also develop Korsakoff's psychosis, a chronic and debilitating syndrome characterized by persistent learning and memory problems. Patients with Korsakoff's psychosis are forgetful and quickly frustrated and have difficulty with walking and coordination
ALCOHOL'S DAMAGING EFFECTS ON THE BRAIN. Alcohol Alert. October 2004

questions.question_text: A 17 year old girl is brought to A&E by ambulance. She appears fascinated by the chair by her bedside, appears to be seeing visual illusions and is talking about the intense experience of hearing the colours around her. Which of the following would be the most likely substance ingested?
questions.explanation:
There are two major classes of psychedelic hallucinogens: the indoleamines (e.g. LSD) and the phenethylamines (e.g. mescaline). LSD is a drug that is taken orally, is rapidly absorbed and effects begin within 1 hour and last for 12 hours. Effects are varied and centre around the distortion of reality. Dependence does not develop to LSD and consequently withdrawal reactions do not occur. Several moods may seem to coexist at the same time. In the longer term, users report 'flashbacks' which is a recurrence of the effects of the drug without having taken any more. They are commonly precipitated by dark environments, fatigue, or cannabis use.
Calvino (1998) American Journal of Nephrology 18(6):565-569. Aghajanian and Marek (1999) Neuropsychopharmacology 21:16S-23S

questions.question_text: The Project Match trial demonstrated that

options.text: Motivational Enhancement Therapy was significantly superior to 12-step approach
12-step approach was significantly superior to Motivational Enhancement Therapy
there was no significant difference in outcome following Motivational Enhancement Therapy, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and 12-step approach
Cognitive Behavioural Therapy was not statistically different to placebo
12-step approach was significantly superior to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy

correct_answer.text: there was no significant difference in outcome following Motivational Enhancement Therapy, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and 12-step approach

correct_answers.text: there was no significant difference in outcome following Motivational Enhancement Therapy, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and 12-step approach

questions.explanation:
Project Match is the largest ever study of psychological interventions for alcohol misuse, and allocated 17000 patients randomly to 3 outpatient treatments.
Project MATCH Research Group. (1993). Project MATCH: Rationale and methods for a multisite clinical trial matching patients to alcoholism treatment. Alcoholism: Clinical and Experimental Research, 17, 1130-1145.

questions.question_text: Interventions with children who live in difficult circumstances should

options.text: wait until a crisis is reached and damage is apparent
focus solely on reducing risk factors
be made only by specialist child and adolescent psychiatrists
involve the professional making a very long-standing commitment to working with the child and their family
start as early as possible in order to promote factors associated with greater resilience

correct_answer.text: start as early as possible in order to promote factors associated with greater resilience

correct_answers.text: start as early as possible in order to promote factors associated with greater resilience

questions.explanation:
There is clear evidence that some children are resilient, and that there are identifiable factors that seem to be associated with both their protection and their resilience. There are two clear ways to promote resilience: by working to reduce the risks to children (the fewer risk factors, the more likely it is that children will not be negatively affected), and by working to increase protective processes and factors (the more of them there are, the more likely it is that children will be resilient).
Velleman & Templeton (2007) Adv Psych Treat 13:79-89

questions.question_text: A 19 year old tells you she takes MDMA. The least likely psychological consequence of this drug is:

options.text: Increased desire to do mental tasks

questions.explanation:
The effects of MDMA include feelings of mental stimulation, emotional warmth, empathy toward others, a general sense of well being, and decreased anxiety. In addition, users report enhanced sensory perception as a hallmark of the MDMA experience.
From National Institute on Drug Abuse, About.com

questions.question_text: A 27 year old man presents with a acute-onset paranoid psychosis with first rank symptoms. Which of the following substances is most likely to produce this picture, and may cause seizures and circulatory collapse at toxic levels?
questions.explanation:
Amphetamine is a stimulant drug, and has many of its effects in common with cocaine. It is taken to produce a 'high', but its side effects include agitation, sleeplessness, anorexia, hypertension and cardiac arrhythmias. At toxic levels there may be seizures and circulatory collapse. Amphetamines produce a paranoid psychosis clinically indistinguishable from schizophrenia. Like cocaine, sudden withdrawal of the drug can lead to a 'crash', with symptoms of agitation, depression, insomnia and anorexia.
Curran et al (2004) BJ Psych 185:196-204

questions.question_text: Which of the following biochemical effects of alcohol has been recognised?

options.text: Craving may be due to dopamine release
Dopamine is released in the nucleus basalis
Potentiation of NMDA receptor channels in glutamate receptor

correct_answer.text: Craving may be due to dopamine release

correct_answers.text: Craving may be due to dopamine release

questions.explanation:
Craving are thought to be due to striatal dopaminergic activity.
Heinz et al (2005) Am J Psych 162: 1515-1520

questions.question_text: You are called to A&E to see someone who has taken PCP. Which of the following would the patient be most likely to exhibit?
questions.explanation:
Muscle contractions may cause uncoordinated movements and bizarre postures. When severe, the muscle contractions can result in bone fracture or in kidney damage or failure as a consequence of muscle cells breaking down. Very high doses of PCP can cause convulsions, coma, hyperthermia, and death.
From National Institute on Drug Abuse, About.com

questions.question_text: What kind of cannabis use has a strong genetic component
questions.explanation:
Genetic risk factors have a moderate impact on the probability of ever using cannabis and a strong impact on the liability to heavy use, abuse, and, probably, dependence. By contrast, the family and social environment substantially influences risk of ever using cannabis but plays little role in the probability of developing heavy cannabis use or abuse.
Kendler and Prescott. Cannabis Use, Abuse, and Dependence in a Population-Based Sample of Female Twins, American Journal of Psychiatry, 1998

questions.question_text: Disulfiram works by

options.text: blocking the action of aldehyde dehydrogenase enzyme

correct_answer.text: blocking the action of aldehyde dehydrogenase enzyme

correct_answers.text: blocking the action of aldehyde dehydrogenase enzyme

questions.explanation:
Disulfiram acts as an aversive agent, by negative reinforcement, through blocking the aldehyde dehydrogenase enzyme that normally metabolises acetaldehyde – this leads to accumulation of acetaldehyde and unpleasant side effects such as flushing, headache, palpitations, nausea and vomiting, even with small intake of alcohol. Larger alcohol intake can lead to hypotension and collapse. Disulfiram should only be prescribed to patients who are physically healthy and understand the possible adverse effects of drinking whilst on the drug.
Revision Notes in Psychiatry - Puri & Hall, 2nd Edition (2004) p348

questions.question_text: In relation to cannabis use and public health, which ONE of the following statements is true?

options.text: preventing cannabis use may lead to reductions in population rates of psychosis
if cannabis use does not cause psychosis then there is no public health justification for preventing cannabis use
recent evidence suggests that cannabis use probably causes more harm to public health than tobacco or alcohol use
there is good evidence that the prohibition of cannabis use is an effective strategy to reduce use among young people
cannabis use appears to have dramatically increased since the recent reclassification of cannabis under the UK Misuse of Drugs Act

correct_answer.text: preventing cannabis use may lead to reductions in population rates of psychosis

correct_answers.text: preventing cannabis use may lead to reductions in population rates of psychosis

questions.explanation: Evidence of an association between cannabis use and psychosis has recently emerged. By normal epidemiological conventions, evidence that this association has a causal basis is currently not strong. However, cannabis may cause psychosis and this possibility presents a tantalising glimpse of a means to effectively reduce the population burden of illnesses such as schizophrenia (McGrath & Saha, 2007).

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following statements is true regarding parental substance misuse?

options.text: it affects children more if the misuser is the mother
it affects children more if the misuse takes place in the family home
it generally has an impact on young children, with adolescents escaping most ill-effects
it reduces the likelihood of violence in the family home
it generally affects only the misuser, and not their children

correct_answer.text: it affects children more if the misuse takes place in the family home

correct_answers.text: it affects children more if the misuse takes place in the family home

questions.explanation: Many children affected by problem substance use within the family environment will reach the attention of social services because of concerns regarding child protection (Forrester & Harwin, 2004). These include the illegal nature of drug misuse, the modes of ingestion, the links to crime, the use of the family home for groups of people to take drugs (drug misuse is more likely to be a home-based activity), and the even stronger links with poverty, unemployment and social deprivation.

questions.question_text: Acamprosate is thought to reduce craving for alcohol by

options.text: functional antagonism of the glutamate NMDA receptor

correct_answer.text: functional antagonism of the glutamate NMDA receptor

correct_answers.text: functional antagonism of the glutamate NMDA receptor

questions.explanation: Acamprosate, in combination with psychosocial therapy, has been shown to be clinically effective in maintaining abstinence in alcohol dependence. Current research suggests that its mechanism of action involves functional antagonism of the ionotropic glutamate N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. However, direct interactions between acamprosate and the NMDA receptor are weak, and recent findings suggest that acamprosate may modulate NMDA receptors via regulatory polyamine sites, or that it may act directly on metabotropic glutamate receptors.

questions.question_text: Therapeutic skills needed to work with the children of substance misusers and the misusing parent

options.text: involve reassurance and risk reduction while referring on to CAMHS or a specialist substance misuse team
require expertise in techniques such as motivational interviewing and relapse prevention
Therapeutic skills needed to work with the children of substance misusers and the misusing parent
take actions and maintain subsequent changes require further training in child psychotherapy and/or family therapy

correct_answer.text: Therapeutic skills needed to work with the children of substance misusers and the misusing parent

correct_answers.text: Therapeutic skills needed to work with the children of substance misusers and the misusing parent

questions.explanation: For work with anyone (adult or child) the clinician needs to: be warm, empathic and genuine; make a therapeutic relationship; help clients to explore their difficulties; enable clients to set achievable goals; empower clients to take action to reach these goals; stay with clients and help them to stabilise and maintain changes. (Velleman & Templeton, 2007)

questions.question_text: You see a 19 year old man in A&E with decreased consciousness, and is unable to give a history. There are needle-marks on his arm. Which of the following clinical features would lead you to suspect opiate overdose?
questions.explanation: An opiate overdose can be a life-threatening emergency. Clinical features include stupor or coma, pinpoint pupils, pallor, severe respiratory depression and pulmonary oedema. (Strang et al. BMJ 2003;326:959-960)

questions.question_text: A 22 year old woman, known to misuse alcohol, gives birth to a baby girl. Which of the following features of the baby would lead you to suspect foetal alcohol syndrome?
questions.explanation: Features of foetal alcohol syndrome include low IQ, cardiac abnormalities, low-set ears, absent philtrum, long thin upper lip, small nose, microcephaly, strabismus and poor growth. (Puri & Hall, Revision Notes in Psychiatry, 2nd Ed, 2004)

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is true regarding substance misuse in the UK?

options.text: 50% of all violent crimes are linked to drug misuse
in the 20-24 age group, survey results suggest that nearly 20% of all women and nearly 10% of all men are drug dependent
liver cirrhosis deaths are rising slower than they are in other western European countries
more people use alcohol hazardously than use drugs hazardously
more people have problems with drugs than with alcohol

correct_answer.text: more people use alcohol hazardously than use drugs hazardously

correct_answers.text: more people use alcohol hazardously than use drugs hazardously

questions.explanation: Around 50% of all violent crimes and, at peak times, up to 70% of all admissions to accident and emergency departments are linked to alcohol misuse. Between 1987-1991 and 1997-2001, deaths from cirrhosis in the UK rose steeply, the highest in western Europe. (Leon & McCambridge, 2006; Velleman & Templeton, 2007)

questions.question_text: 700ml of whisky (40%) contains how many units of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Units of alcohol can be calculated by volume (in litres) multiplied by ABV (Alcohol by Volume in %): 0.7 × 40 = 28 units. (Puri & Hall, Revision Notes in Psychiatry, 1st Ed, 1998)

questions.question_text: With regard to cannabis use and psychotic illness in the UK population over the past 30 years, which ONE of the following statements is true?

options.text: only a small minority of young people today are likely to have used cannabis
rates of psychosis have clearly increased
increasing rates of cannabis use should inevitably have led to increasing rates of psychosis, if cannabis use causes psychosis
rates of psychosis have clearly fallen
most evidence suggests that cannabis use by young people has increased

correct_answer.text: most evidence suggests that cannabis use by young people has increased

correct_answers.text: most evidence suggests that cannabis use by young people has increased

questions.explanation: Since the late 1960s cannabis use has increased substantially in most high-income countries. Cannabis is now the third most widely used psychoactive drug in Europe, the USA and Australasia. In the UK around half of adolescents will use cannabis at least once and about a fifth will use it regularly in young adulthood. (Hickman et al, 2007; Macleod, 2007)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a criteria for Alcohol Dependence?

options.text: damage to physical or mental health

correct_answer.text: damage to physical or mental health

correct_answers.text: damage to physical or mental health

questions.explanation: The ICD-10 criteria for dependence include a strong desire or sense of compulsion to consume alcohol, difficulty in controlling intake, tolerance, withdrawal symptoms, use despite knowledge of harm, and preoccupation with alcohol to exclusion of other activities. Damage to physical or mental health is not a separate criterion. (WHO ICD-10, 1993)

questions.question_text: You are called to see a known opiate user in A&E. Which of the following symptoms would lead you to suspect opioid withdrawal?
questions.explanation: Symptoms of withdrawal from opiates include depression, leg cramps, abdominal cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, insomnia and cravings for the drug itself. (Puri & Hall, Revision Notes in Psychiatry, 2nd Ed, 2004)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding substance misuse and schizophrenia?

options.text: Surveys of psychiatric disorders in the community have reported higher rates of substance abuse disorders among persons with schizophrenia
Alcohol abuse and dependence are more common in the schizophrenic population than in the general population
Rates of alcohol and stimulant use among patients with schizophrenia appear to have remained stable over the last few decades
Cannabis use confers an overall twofold increase in the relative risk for later schizophrenia
Patients with schizophrenia are more likely to have used psychotomimetic drugs such as amphetamines, cocaine, and hallucinogens than other psychiatric patients or normal controls

correct_answer.text: Rates of alcohol and stimulant use among patients with schizophrenia appear to have remained stable over the last few decades

correct_answers.text: Rates of alcohol and stimulant use among patients with schizophrenia appear to have remained stable over the last few decades

questions.explanation: Rates of alcohol and stimulant use among schizophrenic patients have increased over the past several decades, not remained stable. (Schneier & Siris, 1987; Smith & Hucker, 1994; Warner et al., 1994)

questions.question_text: You see a 56 year old man in A&E who appears dishevelled, malnourished and malodorous. Which of the following signs would lead you to suspect Wernicke's encephalopathy?
questions.explanation: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome involves a triad of acute mental confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia due to thiamine deficiency. (Puri & Hall, Revision Notes in Psychiatry, 2nd Ed, 2004)

questions.question_text: EMI Q1 Scenario 1: A 20-year-old man is brought to casualty after suddenly developing the belief that his friends are conspiring to kill him. His pupils are dilated and he is sweating, agitated and tachycardic. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: People intoxicated with amphetamines can develop acute psychotic episodes, which are relatively short lived. Another clue to the diagnosis is the characteristic physical symptoms.

questions.question_text: EMI Q1 Scenario 2: A 45-year-old man of no fixed abode is an inpatient on the medical ward. He is confused, disorientated, shouting, picking up invisible objects off the floor, appears terrified, talking to imaginary people, restless, tremulous and hypertensive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Delirium tremens best fits this clinical picture. The core features are all present, including: clouding of consciousness, bizarre affect, hallucinations, autonomic disturbance and tremor.

questions.question_text: EMI Q1 Scenario 3: A young woman is brought to casualty having been arrested for shoplifting. She became unwell in custody, complaining of severe abdominal cramps and muscle and joint pain. In the department she appears restless, sweats profusely and has 'goose bumps.' What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical picture is one of opioid withdrawal. The woman will not have had access to drugs while in custody and has developed withdrawal symptoms. Shoplifting may have been to finance her addiction.

questions.question_text: EMI Q2 Scenario 1: A 30-year-old man, dependent on alcohol, comes to A&E with a head wound. He is homeless and becomes agitated in the department. He experiences seeing squirrels crawling over the floor. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The visual hallucinations are most suggestive of delirium tremens.

questions.question_text: EMI Q2 Scenario 2: The same 45-year-old inpatient has two abscesses in his groin and neck, small pupils and bradycardia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: These features are suggestive of opiate overdose intoxication.

questions.question_text: EMI Q2 Scenario 3: He doesn’t recognise the left side of his body. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This hemi-neglect is most likely to have been caused by an intracranial bleed.

questions.question_text: EMI Q3 Scenario 1: A 40-year-old opiate dependent woman wants to become abstinent but cannot tolerate withdrawal symptoms. Which treatment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Lofexidine is an alpha-2 agonist like clonidine used in the management of opioid withdrawal.

questions.question_text: EMI Q3 Scenario 2: A 35-year-old man wants to stop using IV heroin but does not want methadone. Which treatment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine is used in substitution treatment of opioid dependence when methadone is not wanted.

questions.question_text: EMI Q3 Scenario 3: A 22-year-old patient on outpatient methadone collapses in the clinic with pinpoint pupils and tachycardia. Which treatment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Naloxone reverses the effects of heroin in opioid overdose.

questions.question_text: EMI Q4 Scenario 1: An 18-year-old man has a two-month history of panic attacks, anxiety and vivid flashbacks. He has become withdrawn and shown inappropriate behaviour. On examination he has conjunctival injection and a cough. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Social withdrawal, change of behaviour, respiratory symptoms and red eyes are suggestive of cannabis use.

questions.question_text: EMI Q4 Scenario 2: A 45-year-old man of no fixed abode is confused, shouting, picking up invisible objects, restless, tremulous and hypertensive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This acute confusion and visual hallucinations in a dishevelled man are suggestive of delirium tremens.

questions.question_text: EMI Q4 Scenario 3: A 19-year-old man with polysubstance abuse sweats profusely, appears agitated and claims to see the colour red while listening to his CDs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The physiological arousal and synaesthetic features suggest LSD use.

questions.question_text: EMI Q5 Scenario 1: A 32-year-old opiate dependent woman in the second trimester of pregnancy wants to stop using heroin but is scared of withdrawal symptoms. Which treatment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Methadone is the only medication currently licensed for opioid detox or substitution treatment in pregnancy.

questions.question_text: EMI Q5 Scenario 2: A 45-year-old man has recently finished opioid detoxification. He seeks treatment to help him stop heroin but is not keen on substitution. Which treatment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Naltrexone, an opioid antagonist, is used to prevent relapse in people who have completed detox and don’t want substitution treatment.

questions.question_text: EMI Q5 Scenario 3: A 22-year-old man on outpatient methadone is found unconscious, tachycardic with pinpoint pupils. Which treatment is most likely?
questions.explanation: Naloxone reverses the effects of heroin in opioid overdose.

questions.question_text: The following are NOT considered to be steps of Evidence based practice

options.text: Conducting a RCT, if evidence unavailable

correct_answer.text: Conducting a RCT, if evidence unavailable

correct_answers.text: Conducting a RCT, if evidence unavailable

questions.explanation: The steps in Evidence based Psychiatry include: Formulating a clinical question, Searching for evidence, Critically appraising the validity and applicability of the study, Applying this on the patient and finally Auditing your practice.

questions.question_text: Cochrane reviews constitute which grade of evidence?
questions.explanation: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses are considered Type Ia evidence. Cochrane reviews are robust systematic reviews, hence are considered Type Ia evidence.

questions.question_text: A Consultant Psychiatrist wanting to provide evidence-based prescribing for a patient with bipolar depression finds a credible RCT. The next step in their quest for Evidence based practice would be:

options.text: Providing the article for the patient to decide if she wanted the treatment
Auditing the use of this treatment in the hospital
Speaking to colleagues about the value of the treatment advocated in the article
Deciding on the validity and applicability of the study
Talking to patient user groups about the proposed treatment

correct_answer.text: Deciding on the validity and applicability of the study

correct_answers.text: Deciding on the validity and applicability of the study

questions.explanation: The steps in Evidence based Psychiatry include: Formulating a clinical question, Searching for evidence, Critically appraising the validity and applicability of the study, Applying this on the patient and finally Auditing your practice.

questions.question_text: The database that provides systematic coverage of the psychological literature from the 1800s to the present is
questions.explanation: PsycINFO is an abstract database that provides systematic coverage of the psychological literature from the 1800s to the present, including bibliographic citations, abstracts, cited references, and descriptive information across behavioral and social sciences.

questions.question_text: The best evidence for planning services is usually derived from
questions.explanation: The most useful evidence in service planning comes from quantitative systematic reviews of key parameters such as prevalence, incidence, utilisation data and service delivery methods. (Chipps et al., 2000)

questions.question_text: The following is true of practice of evidence based psychiatry

options.text: Cannot be done in the absence of systematic reviews
Includes assessing the scientific validity and clinical importance of evidence
Is only concerned with medical treatment
Recommends treatments based on evidence from RCTs
Is not impacted by a psychiatrist’s clinical experience

correct_answer.text: Includes assessing the scientific validity and clinical importance of evidence

correct_answers.text: Includes assessing the scientific validity and clinical importance of evidence

questions.explanation: The steps in Evidence based Psychiatry include: Formulating a clinical question, Searching for evidence, Critically appraising the validity and applicability of the study, Applying this on the patient and finally Auditing your practice.

questions.question_text: The following is True regarding searching for evidence during the process of EBM

options.text: A literature search is best preceded by a formulation of a four-part clinical question
Medline covers most of the published treatment studies in a given field
NICE guidelines are based on robust systematic reviews
Clinical guidelines are best derived from consensus meetings
When searching for evidence on treatment trials, looking for RCTs provide the best search strategy

correct_answer.text: A literature search is best preceded by a formulation of a four-part clinical question

correct_answers.text: A literature search is best preceded by a formulation of a four-part clinical question

questions.explanation: A literature search is best preceded by a four-part clinical question (PICO: Patient, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome). Clinical guidelines should be based on systematic reviews, and Medline covers only 40–60% of published literature, so multiple databases are recommended.

questions.question_text: The following are true of case-control studies

options.text: Measures the exposure and the outcome prospectively
Can evaluate multiple outcomes of a single exposure

questions.explanation: Case-control studies compare subjects with and without a disease on prior exposure. They are relatively easy to conduct, can investigate many exposures, and are particularly suitable for studying rare diseases, but are prone to bias and confounding because exposure is assessed retrospectively. (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding RCT is True

options.text: Blinding creates two otherwise equal groups
Randomisation distributes confounders equally between groups

correct_answer.text: Randomisation distributes confounders equally between groups

correct_answers.text: Randomisation distributes confounders equally between groups

questions.explanation: Randomisation provides two more or less identical groups in terms of both known and unknown confounders, and concealed randomisation prevents investigators from selectively assigning patients to treatment groups. (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about RCT is False

options.text: It is the best study design for generalising results to the population at large
Considered as the gold standard for evaluating treatment
The number needed to treat can be calculated
Reduces bias by comparison of otherwise equal groups

correct_answer.text: It is the best study design for generalising results to the population at large

correct_answers.text: It is the best study design for generalising results to the population at large

questions.explanation: While RCTs are the gold standard for evaluating treatment and minimise confounders, they are often not the best design for generalising results to the wider population (external validity). (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)

questions.question_text: An evaluation of a new screening questionnaire for depression in primary care is conducted. The most important single feature of this questionnaire that would encourage you to use it is:

options.text: It is validated in different languages
It has a positive predictive value of 20%

questions.explanation: A screening instrument is selected on the basis of having high sensitivity and specificity. In this example, a sensitivity of 80% suggests the instrument will correctly identify 80% of true cases, which is a crucial measure of utility. (Altman & Bland, BMJ, 1994)

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding Experimental Clinical trials

options.text: Tend to overestimate the benefits of experimental treatments in the absence of control groups
Randomisation is required to minimise bias
Are most reliable if conducted pragmatically

correct_answer.text: Tend to overestimate the benefits of experimental treatments in the absence of control groups

correct_answers.text: Tend to overestimate the benefits of experimental treatments in the absence of control groups

questions.explanation: The simplest clinical trial is open or uncontrolled, and these habitually overestimate the beneficial effects of an experimental treatment by an average of 20%. (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)

questions.question_text: A curve with plot of sensitivity versus 1-specificity on either axis is
questions.explanation: The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve is a plot of the true positive rate (sensitivity) versus the false positive rate (1 – specificity) for all possible cut points. (Obuchowski, Radiology, 2003)

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be used to evaluate the possibility of publication bias in a systematic review?
questions.explanation: Funnel plots were devised to evaluate the possibility of publication bias, but can also evaluate potential sources of heterogeneity. (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)

questions.question_text: A researcher is interested to understand why some people adapt so well to chronic illness whereas many find it difficult to cope. The study design best suited to answer their question would be
questions.explanation: Qualitative research is concerned with personal meanings, experiences, feelings, values and other types of opinion. The data are usually gathered with semi-structured interviews or focus groups, generating hypotheses for further testing. (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)

questions.question_text: The cost of forgoing an established treatment whilst opting for a new treatment is termed as
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost is best measured by the health benefits (life years saved, QALYs gained) that could have been achieved had the money been spent on the next best alternative intervention. (Palmer & Raftery, BMJ, 1999)

questions.question_text: Case reports and case series are types of which study?
questions.explanation: Case reports and series, audits, qualitative studies, cross-sectional and ecological studies are descriptive observational studies. (Lawrie, McIntosh & Rao, 2000)
